candidates.reason: sys_rt_sigaction() copies the whole struct sigaction from user memory once via copy_from_user(&new_sa.sa, act, sizeof(new_sa.sa)) into kernel struct new_sa and passes only the kernel copy to do_sigaction(); there is no second fetch of *act before use, so no validate/use divergence (lines 4425-4430).

setxattr_copy() copies the user xattr name once into ctx->kname->name via strncpy_from_user and all later consumers (do_setxattr/vfs_setxattr) read the kernel copy; the apparent duplicate copy_from_user hits from the scanner are two independent syscall entry points, not a double fetch of the same location.

hpsa_big_passthru_ioctl() fetches the fixed BIG_IOCTL_Command_struct header once (copy_from_user at drivers/scsi/hpsa.c:6662) and then loops copy_from_user(buff[sg_used], data_ptr, sz) per SG chunk; sz/left are kernel copies, but the per-iteration user data_ptr advance walks user-controlled buffer contents and post-completion copy_to_user/err_info paths re-read user memory; cannot fully rule out a validate/use divergence on the same user locations within the time window, but no single field is provably validated on one fetch and used from a second fetch of the same address.

ethtool ioctl handlers copy each struct from useraddr once (e.g. copy_from_user(&cmd, useraddr, sizeof(cmd)) then copy_from_user(features, useraddr, sizeof(features))) into distinct kernel structures; the repeated useraddr fetches are sequential reads of different offsets of the user blob, not a second fetch of a previously validated field, and all decisions use the kernel copies.

uinput_ioctl_handler copies setup/ff structs from arg/buffer once into kernel locals before validation and use; the multiple copy_from_user calls are for different commands (UI_DEV_SETUP vs force-feedback upload/erase), each single-fetch into a local.

ip_setsockopt() fetches each optval variant (mreq/greq/gsf/msf/val) once into a kernel local and validates/uses the local; compat paths (gr32/gf32) fetch once as well; no re-fetch of the same user location after validation.

userfaultfd ioctl handlers use copy_from_user into kernel structs (uffdio_copy/zeropage/register/wake) with deliberately partial copies to exclude the 'copy' field; each user location is fetched once and kernel copies are used; copy_to_user of results is a distinct direction.

privcmd mmapbatch ioctls fetch struct m once per ioctl variant; the two copy_from_user calls belong to separate PRIVCMD_MMAPBATCH and PRIVCMD_MMAPBATCH_V2 cases, each single-fetch into kernel struct before use.

io_submit iocb lookup copies struct iocb from user_iocb once (copy_from_user(&iocb, user_iocb, sizeof(iocb))) and passes the kernel copy into aio; however aio iocb user pointers remain in user memory and are re-fetched on completion (write-back of results to the user iocb), a pattern double-fetch audits flag, but the later access is a result write-back rather than a validated-then-used value; not classified as a violation of the single-fetch invariant.

ethtool_rxfh handlers read rxfh.indir_size/hkey_size from the once-copied kernel struct rxfh, then copy indir/hkey blobs from computed offsets; user_size is read via copy_from_user once and compared; blob copies are of distinct offsets, not re-fetches of validated scalars.

limitations: The scan was a whole-tree static heuristic over ~126KB of raw candidate functions (persisted scan output) matching multiple get_user/copy_from_user-family calls per function with a shared user pointer token; only the ten highest-signal candidates above were deeply read, covering the largest kernel-subsystem hit clusters (signal, xattr, uapi setsockopt, ioctls, uinput, aio, userfaultfd, hpsa, ethtool).

Remaining unexamined hit clusters from the same scan include arch/*/kernel/signal*.c sigreturn frame multi-fetches (sigframe parsing in arch/m68k, arch/mips, arch/s390, arch/powerpc, etc.), drivers/vhost/vhost.c, net/sctp/socket.c, net/ipv6/ip6mr.c, drivers/comedi/comedi_fops.c, and sound/pci/emu10k1/emufx.c; each has multiple copy_from_user calls but was not deeply read within this intent's budget.
tools/testing/selftests/* hits were excluded as userspace test code, not kernel attack surface.

No runtime reproducer or compiler-based double-fetch detector was run; classification relies on manual reading of fetch sites and use sites, so a short-window double fetch inside a large function could have been missed.
